messages:
emily: quick sync after the onboarding smoke this morning. saw two weird failure patterns we should capture in the pipeline.

ryan: details?

emily: 1) model wheel serialized fine but runtime threw an unexpected kernel mismatch (fused attention op missing in recent image). 2) perf cliff on certain long-form prompts due to kv-cache fragmentation across shards.

dee: for (1) are we sure it's fused-op absence and not a different ABI flag? logs showed vkern_unavailable on load.

emily: vendor log shows mismatch: wheel used aten::fused_attn, image has aten::attn_unfused only. fallback path allocates huge temp buffers and OOMs.

tasha: hmm. we've been relying on ABI + dtype checks at admit. need an op-level compatibility check.

ryan: thought: emit an op-list during wheel build (simple extraction), store it in model metadata, and compare to image capability index at admission time.

dee: yep. infra could publish image capability manifests during image promotion. that avoids spinning containers.

infra-bot: INFRA: scheduled task idea logged as ticket INFRA-872 (image capability export).

emily: op-list extraction might be flaky for traced graphs with dynamic dispatch; we should support a manual override in manifest: "required_ops": ["aten::fused_attn"] for authors.

tasha: add a confidence flag: "ops_inferred": true/false so validator warns if inferred only.

ryan: about (2) kv-cache fragmentation: microbench uses short prompts. we need to include a small suite of long-form probes that exercise cross-chunk attention and high prefix reuse.

emily: propose new probe type 'longtail' with 5-10 canonical long prompts plus randomized suffixes. not a full bench but heavier than microbench.

dee: cost concern: running longtail on every ingest increases spend. maybe staged execution: admit via microbench, schedule longtail async, block production route until pass, permit canary traffic.

tasha: that aligns with staged-admit idea. also record probe-suite version in model entry so we can track regressions.

ryan: we should also include a per-probe deterministic seed and store probe-hashes in registry. simplifies diffs later.

emily: agree. probe artifact record example: "probe_suite":"longtail-v1","probe_hashes":["h1","h2",...]. store as strings.

infra-bot: NOTE: added config suggestion -> control-plane should expose image capabilities at /v1/images/{tag}/capabilities.

dee: UX: when validator rejects, message should be actionable: include missing ops + recommended remediation steps (rebuild with unfused ops, request new image, or change quant scheme).

tasha: also add an automated fallback rule: if missing fused op but an unfused equivalent exists, we can map to fallback variant and mark as degraded with a mitigation note.

ryan: one more thing: transient infra variance. image capability may change between detection and runtime if node pools differ. consider a runtime check at first canary start to confirm capabilities.

emily: yes, maybe a lightweight runtime probe on canary start that exercises a small op set. failover to safe variant if mismatch.

dee: acceptance criteria for these changes?

emily: 1) validator stores inferred op-list and compares against image index, warning on mismatch. 2) manifest supports required_ops and ops_inferred fields. 3) longtail probes added, probe_suite/version recorded and probe hashes persisted. 4) infra publishes image capabilities API. 5) canary runtime probe on first healthy start.

tasha: owners: emily -> probe changes + UX, ryan -> op-list extractor + manifest schema, infra -> image capability API, dee -> canary runtime probe.

ryan: i can prototype op-list extractor tomorrow. will post a short PR with examples.

emily: thanks, team. let's record these in the RFC follow-up doc and review Friday. if anyone wants to sketch error messages ping me.

tasha: :raised_hands: cool.
